key_insight: BiLoGo combines local FE-mesh learning with global Transformer communication to reduce smoothing of critical, localised sheet-forming responses.
engineering_relevance: More accurate localisation of thinning near ribs and sharp radii could improve learned simulators used to accelerate sheet-forming design.
method: Bidirectional node–element GraphSAGE predicts quantities on their native FE entities without interpolation.
Dual-stream Transformer tokens separate blank deformation from tool contact information.
Gated residual fusion combines local and global features, with element updates conditioned on element–node kinematics.
evidence_signal: Across three forming cases, BiLoGo achieved the lowest positional and threshold-based thinning errors among tested models; near ribs, BiLoGo-U raised the thinning smoothing index to 0.94 versus 0.41–0.56 for Transformer baselines.
watch_item: Evaluation covers three forming cases; generalisation to broader geometries, materials and process conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: BiLoGo: Reducing the smoothing of localised responses in Transformer-based neural operators for sheet forming
